Entries.Text: What this view edits: textures (TPF containers), or the menu and HUD screens (Scaleform .gfx movies).
The texture containers, by category. The File List, Texture List, Viewer and Properties show the selected TPF and texture.
The menu and HUD screens (Scaleform .gfx movies). Selecting one opens it: the File List shows its display list, the Texture List its images, the Viewer its stage, and Properties the selected element.
Select a movie in the Container List.

The instances on the stage at the shown frame: [depth] instance name (character). Sprites hold their own timelines. Greyed instances are not drawn (hidden, masks, transparent, or inside one of those).
Shows every instance hidden in the preview.
Hides everything in the preview (the eye toggles show them again).

Shows or hides this instance and what is inside it in the preview. Preview only: the movie is not changed.

Shift+click: every instance of the same character takes the same state.

Hidden by an instance above it. Click to hide it on its own as well.

Shift+click: every instance of the same character takes the same state.

The external images of the movie. The game finds each .tga name as a cell of a shoebox layout (sblytbnd) of the same name, in the TPF beside the layout, or as a texture of that name in the menu TPFs. Red: not found.
Looks the images up again: after editing a layout or a menu TPF, or changing files outside Smithbox.
No shoebox cell or menu texture has this name.
The selected instance. Moves apply to the keyframes of its animation track (see Move whole animation); scale and rotation to the keyframe shown.
Instance names and frame labels are read-only by default. The game finds elements by instance-name path (PlayerHUD/Gauge/AP_Gauge) and plays states by frame label.
Renaming an instance or a label the game uses breaks that screen without an error: the game just stops finding it.
Click an element on the stage, or an instance in the Display List.
The instance name. The game finds elements by it.
The instance-name path from the root, as the game addresses it; unnamed levels as [depth]. Right-click to copy.
The timeline the instance is placed on. An instance inside a sprite symbol is shared: editing it changes every use of that symbol.
Sprite {0}, used {1} times: edits change every use
Effects the stage does not draw yet. They are kept in the file as they are.
Mask for the depths up to {0} (not drawn)
On: a move shifts every keyframe of the instance's animation track, so the animation plays where you put it. Off: only the keyframe shown moves, which changes the animation's path.
Position in the parent's space, in pixels.
Applies to the keyframe shown only. Skew is not kept.
Where the instance and its contents are on the stage, in pixels.
Colour = colour x Mult / 256 + Add, per channel. Edits the keyframe that set the colour (else the one shown).
Sprite {0}: {1} frame(s), placed {2} time(s). The frame shown applies to every use of this sprite.
The frame this sprite is shown at (preview only; the game picks it at runtime).
The game plays states by frame label.
A text field definition: edits change every instance of it. The game sets the shown text at runtime, so the initial text is mostly a placeholder.
The text box in the instance's space, in pixels.
The text in the file (HTML for HTML fields). The game usually replaces it.
An image definition: edits change every instance of it.
The image the game shows: a shoebox cell or menu texture of this name (the .tga extension is not looked at).
DefineShape{0}, first fill: {1} {2}. The stage draws the shape's bounds with its first fill.
Fits the stage in the window.

Click: select the element (its nearest named instance). Ctrl+click: the image, text or shape itself. Drag: move. Escape while dragging: cancel. Arrows: nudge 1 px (Shift: 10). Backspace: select the parent. Wheel: zoom. Middle drag or Space+drag: pan.
{0}: {1} tag(s) could not be decoded and are kept as they are (not editable).
Failed to read the menu TPF {0} for the movie images
The movie edit failed and was undone

Images to show in the GFx mode's preview in place of placeholders: images the game fills in at runtime (MENU_Icon_00000, EquipPanel_00001) or that no atlas has. Preview only: the movies are not changed. Saved with the project.
The image name in the movie, without its extension (MENU_Icon_00000). * matches any characters (EquipPanel_*). An exact name wins over a pattern; of two patterns, the more specific one wins.
A shoebox cell or menu texture name to show instead. Type part of a name to pick from the names the preview knows.
No shoebox cell or menu texture has this name; the placeholder keeps its outline.
Adds the substitute, or changes the one for this placeholder. Saved at once.
Open a movie (Container List in GFX mode) to list its placeholders.
Every image of this movie is found.
Not found. Click to use it as the placeholder.
Failed to read the Scaleform Configuration {0}
Failed to write the Scaleform Configuration {0}
